subject.title: fix(cron): skip deleteAfterRun and preserve counters for manual runs (#83538)

question: Should public `cron run` permanently become non-consuming for `deleteAfterRun` one-shots and scheduler retry state, with consumption reserved for timer and gateway watcher execution?
rationale: This is a compatibility-sensitive change to an existing public operator workflow; source evidence supports the safer non-destructive default, but the permanent semantic contract needs maintainer intent.

options.title: Adopt non-consuming operator runs
options.body: Keep the branch's boundary: manual runs record outcomes but preserve scheduler-owned deletion, counters, backoff, and next-run state.

options.title: Preserve consuming manual runs
options.body: Retain current behavior or require a separately designed explicit opt-in for non-consuming verification runs, accepting the existing destructive workflow.

recommendation.title: Adopt non-consuming operator runs
recommendation.body: Keep the branch's boundary: manual runs record outcomes but preserve scheduler-owned deletion, counters, backoff, and next-run state.

likelyOwner.reason: Recent merged work owns the adjacent due-slot and recomputation invariants that determine whether this compatibility direction remains scheduler-safe.
